historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR (6.4%) haircut for FY26's +0.4% and US unit share loss; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 20.8% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr 6.4% and EPS 3yr 6.0%. Book growth is retained cash (net cash rose from ~0.65bn FY21 to 4.5bn FY26 while ~no buybacks until FY26), not business growth, so the equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF deducts SBC incl. withholding taxes and, from FY2023 (first net-interest-income year), interest income: FY23 65.9m, FY24 145.7m, FY25 178.9m, FY26 181.9m (XBRL InterestIncomeExpenseNonoperatingNet; FY21-22 were net expense, nothing deducted). The owner-FCF CAGR runs ~2pp below reported, and that gap is the growing interest income, not SBC: SBC is flat at ~0.8-1.0% of revenue. FY26 FCF is flattered by 7.2% capex (vs 12-14%) and depressed by an 80m receivables build and 97m of tax receivable/payable swings. Revenue growth decelerated from 30% (FY22) to 0.4% (FY26).

scenario_narratives.base: Copart ex-ACV stabilises: US insurance units flatten after FY26's ~-2.8% as the Progressive reallocation to IAA annualises, while ASP gains and the international segment (units +10%, revenue +11.7% in Q4 FY26) bring organic revenue growth back to ~5% before fading to 3%. Margin recovers only partially (41% pre-SBC EBITDA vs 42-44% in FY22-24) because IAA has closed the cycle-time gap. Capex normalises to ~10% of revenue then tapers. ACV, acquired 2026-10-16, is carried in the bridge at its unaffected market value, so the ~0.59bn premium is charged as value paid away and the leadership change (Liaw out, founder Adair back) is treated as neutral to the organic path.
scenario_narratives.bull: The secular total-loss-frequency tailwind (repair-cost inflation from ADAS/electronics outrunning used-vehicle values) reasserts itself, Copart's land bank and catastrophe surge capacity win back insurer share under the founder who built that lead, and international becomes a second engine. Automation takes pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to ~43.5%. Growth peaks at 7.5% and fades to 3.5%, 20x exit. ACV earning more than its unaffected market value is upside outside the flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: The moat erodes into a price-competitive duopoly: IAA's turnaround (cycle times ~7 days shorter, backlog -20%) keeps winning national-carrier assignments, Copart cuts fees to hold volume, organic revenue shrinks in FY27 and grows ~3% thereafter, and margin settles at 36.5%. Used-car price normalisation cuts ASP-linked fees. Management attention is split between an unplanned CEO change, a new President structure and the largest acquisition in the company's history, and ACV becomes a multi-year drag (not in the flows). 15x exit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict owner basis: SBC and withholding taxes expensed, share count flat, interest income stripped with the 4.5bn July cash and T-bill portfolio added in the bridge, and the now-completed all-cash ACV purchase charged at its premium over ACV's unaffected value. The key judgment is margin: whether the Q4 FY26 compression (pre-SBC EBITDA 38% vs 42-44% historically) is the new competitive equilibrium with a resurgent IAA or a transitory mix and G&A effect. This update refreshes anchors only; the driver paths wait for the first post-ACV, post-CEO-change quarter.
key_risks_to_valuation: National-carrier concentration: further reallocations like Progressive's to IAA would push results toward the bear path
Margin: the 41% base recovery assumes the Q4 FY26 compression partly reverses; if 38% is the new level, base value falls materially

ACV (closed 2026-10-16): valued at unaffected market value with no synergies; losses beyond management's 'breakeven year one' guidance are not modelled, and no purchase-price allocation or segment result has been published yet
Capex normalisation: FY26's 7.2% capex flatters reported FCF; a return to FY22-FY25's 12-14% land-bank spend would cut owner FCF by ~200-300m/yr
Used-vehicle price cycle: ASP-linked fees and purchased-vehicle margins are cyclical
Interest income on the cash pile (~182m/yr) is excluded from flows; the value is carried as cash, so deploying it below the 9% WACC (as ACV's premium suggests) destroys value relative to this model
Leadership: unplanned CEO change effective 2026-07-31 (founder Jay Adair returning) plus a newly created President role, coinciding with the ACV integration; no quantified effect in the paths
Anchor vintage: balance sheet is 2026-07-31 (pre-ACV); Q1 FY2027 results expected ~2026-11-23 will reset net cash, share count and the year-1 path

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation 38,818k + payments for employee stock-based tax withholdings 3,736k (financing). Copart publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two are summed. Filing units are thousands; converted to millions.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 926.33m basic shares outstanding at 2026-09-25 (FY2026 10-K cover; 926.30m at 2026-07-31, so no repurchases since year-end) plus ~6.0m of dilution = 932.3m. Dilution by treasury-stock method at the current price: 12.76m service options at a $24.19 average strike (~2.95m), 4.45m performance options at $22.97 (~1.20m), 1.84m unvested RSUs. Ties to the Q4 FY2026 diluted weighted average (932.14m) used in the prior version. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The FY2026 buyback (1.63bn, 43.4m shares) funded the flat count; the ACV deal was all cash, so no acquisition-currency issuance.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.0%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Same 9% in all scenarios: risk is charged through the probability-weighted driver paths, not a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost sits inside facility operations, i.e. inside EBITDA. Lease liabilities (88.4m) therefore excluded from net debt. One treatment, not two. Copart owns most of its yard land, so leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable non-controlling interest 16.6m (July 2026 balance sheet) deducted in the equity bridge; NCI share of losses (-3.9m FY26) is immaterial to the flows.
inputs.net_cash_note: Net cash = cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash 1,907.9m + held-to-maturity T-bills (current) 2,581.9m - zero borrowings (the 1.25bn 2026 revolver is undrawn) = 4,489.8m at 2026-07-31, the latest filed balance sheet (FY2026 10-K). That date is BEFORE the ACV close (2026-10-16), so the ~1.9bn paid is deducted in the equity bridge; pro-forma net cash is ~2.6bn before Q1 FY2027 cash generation. Interest income (181.9m FY26) is stripped from the FCF base and excluded from the component build so the cash pile is counted once, in the bridge. Replace this anchor with the 2026-10-31 balance sheet when the Q1 FY2027 10-Q is filed (results expected ~2026-11-23) and drop the ACV cash line from the bridge at that point, or the cash is deducted twice.
inputs.acv_treatment: ACV Auctions acquisition COMPLETED 2026-10-16 (cash tender at $10.50/share, ~68.4% tendered then merged; ~1.9bn funded from cash on hand, revolver undrawn). Treatment is deliberately unchanged from the 2026-09-26 version, with 'pending' now 'paid': the latest filed balance sheet (2026-07-31) still holds the cash, so the bridge deducts the ~1.9bn consideration and adds ACV at its UNAFFECTED market value (~1.31bn, consideration / 1.45), i.e. the ~0.59bn premium is charged as value paid away and no synergies are credited. ACV's revenue and losses are NOT in the driver paths: growth_rates are Copart ex-ACV (organic). Reported FY2027 revenue will therefore run well ahead of the model's year-1 growth (roughly three-quarters of a year of ACV, a ~750m-revenue business, on a 4.67bn base); that gap is consolidation, not a forecast miss. Putting ACV through the flows instead would require a separate lower-margin segment build for a historically loss-making business on which Copart has not yet published a purchase-price allocation or segment results (10-K Note 19: accounting evaluation not complete). What would move it: the Q1 FY2027 10-Q (purchase accounting, ACV segment revenue and operating loss, any assumed ACV debt or finance receivables) and updated accretion guidance from the Q1 call. Management guidance remains breakeven contribution in year one, accretive from FY2028.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 1: operating company, US, fee-based marketplace; no bank/REIT/holdco features; the HTM portfolio is corporate treasury, not a lending book). UPDATE of the 2026-09-26 first valuation; same model, see top-level update_review and reconciliation. FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 31 July 2026). The prior version took FY0 from the 2026-09-10 earnings release; the FY2026 10-K is now on file and its cash flow statement, balance sheet and segment note confirm every FY0 anchor unchanged (capex 337.4m, SBC 38.8m, withholding 3.7m, interest income 181.9m, D&A ex debt costs 229.4m, cash 1,907.9m, HTM 2,581.9m, redeemable NCI 16.6m, buybacks 1,632.5m). FY26: revenue 4,666.2m (+0.4%), operating income 1,652.6m, D&A 229.4m, SBC 38.8m, so pre-SBC EBITDA 1,920.8m = 41.2% (FY25 42.0%, FY24 42.4%, FY23 43.6%; Q4 FY26 alone 38.2%). OCF 1,604.5m, capex 337.4m (7.2% of revenue, unusually low vs 12-14% FY22-FY25 land-bank years). Reported FCF 1,267.1m; owner FCF = 1,267.1 - 42.6 SBC incl. withholding - 181.9 interest income = 1,042.7m. The component build does not carry FY26's low capex forward: capex is modelled at 10% of revenue near-term, tapering. Cash taxes paid 398.4m FY26 on ~1.84bn pre-tax = ~21.7%, consistent with the 21.5% path. Buybacks: 1.63bn in FY26 after none FY20-FY25, none since year-end (share count flat July to late September), so the flat count is funded by a repurchaser whose capacity the ACV cash outlay has reduced. The price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print; note that Q1 FY2027 results (first quarter consolidating ACV, first under returning CEO Jay Adair) are expected ~2026-11-23 and will supersede both the price and the balance-sheet anchors. FY2026 is missing from core_metrics/Metrics.csv (stops at Q3 FY2026); FY0 figures come from the 10-K text, not backfilled here (US filer; the XBRL route owns that).

bear.narrative: The duopoly turns price-competitive: IAA's operational turnaround and the Progressive shift spread to other national carriers, US units keep falling and Copart concedes seller fees to hold volume. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 36.5% (Q4 FY26 was 38.2% with gross profit -5.5%), a 15x exit for a structurally slower business. Used-car price normalisation hits ASP-linked fees and purchased-vehicle margins. ACV, now owned, losing money beyond FY2027 while a new CEO and a new President structure integrate it would be further downside not captured in the flows.

base.narrative: Copart ex-ACV. US insurance units stabilise after the FY26 decline as Progressive's reallocation to IAA annualises; pricing (ASP) and international (+10% units) carry growth back to ~5% mid-decade, fading to 3%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin starts at 39.5% (FY26 41.2%, Q4 run-rate 38.2%) and recovers only to 41% on automation, below the 42-44% of FY22-FY24. Capex normalises to 10% of revenue (FY26's 7.2% not carried forward) and tapers to 8% as land-bank build slows. Path unchanged from 2026-09-26: no guidance or results have been published since.

bull.narrative: Total-loss frequency keeps rising (ADAS/electronics repair cost vs used-car values), Copart wins back share from IAA on cycle time and buyer depth, and the international export network (38% of units, 46% of dollars to international buyers) compounds at double digits. Automation lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to the FY24 level (~43.5%). Capex stays higher to fund the growth. Returning founder-CEO Jay Adair's stated priorities (international salvage, US whole-car, technology services) are this path. ACV synergies (cross-sell to dealers, shared logistics) would add to it but are not in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 25/50/25 after review. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: FY26 brought measurable share loss to IAA (units -2.8% vs IAA +4.7%), a Q4 profitability miss (operating income -10.6%), and concentration in a handful of national carriers, one of which (Progressive) has already shifted volume. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (share regained, margin back to FY24, international compounding). Base held at 50%. The CEO change (Jeff Liaw out 2026-07-31, founder Jay Adair back; not known to the prior version) was considered and does not move the weights: an unplanned exit two years in, concurrent with the ACV integration, is an execution risk, but the successor ran the company from 2010 to 2024 and no operating result has yet been reported under him, so it cuts both ways and the bear weight already sits 10 points above default for operating reasons. The balance sheet (4.5bn net cash at July, ~2.6bn after ACV, no debt) still rules out a solvency tail, so bear is margin compression, not distress. Q1 FY2027 results (~2026-11-23) are the first evidence that could shift these.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
